items.stem: A student burns 10 g of ethanol in an open beaker. After the reaction, no residue is left in the beaker. Does this mean the Law of Conservation of Mass is violated? Explain.
items.answer: No, the Law of Conservation of Mass is not violated in this reaction. When ethanol burns, it reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide gas and water vapour, which escape into the atmosphere because the beaker is open. If the reaction were conducted in a closed system and the mass of the escaping gases was measured along with the oxygen consumed, the total mass of the reactants would equal the total mass of the products.

items.stem: When 20 g of hydrogen reacts completely with 160 g of oxygen, how much water is formed according to the Law of Conservation of Mass?
items.answer: According to the Law of Conservation of Mass, the total mass of the product (water) will be equal to the total mass of the reactants, which is 20 g of hydrogen plus 160 g of oxygen. Therefore, 180 g of water is formed. 3. A compound consists of 40% sulfur and 60% oxygen by mass. In a sample of the same compound containing 20 g of sulfur, what mass of oxygen must be present to satisfy the Law of Constant Proportions? Atomic Foundations of Matter CHAPTER 9 Atomic Foundations of Matter SSummar 1. Law of conservation of mass Antoine Lavoisier established the law of conservation of mass. According to this law, there is no loss or gain in mass during a chemical or physical change. In other words, matter can neither be created nor destroyed. 2. Law of Constant Proportion This law was given by French chemist Joseph Proust. It states that every pure compound contains the same elements combined in the same proportion by mass. That means, the chemical composition of a compound is definite, so, this law is also termed as law of constant composition or definite proportion. 3. Dalton’s atomic theory John Dalton used two fundamental laws of chemical combination, i.e., the law of conservation of mass and law of constant proportion for his atomic theory. The assumptions of Dalton’s atomic theory are as follows : 1. All forms of matter are composed of very small discrete particles called atoms. 2. An atom cannot be further broken down into still simpler particles. 3. Atoms can neither be created nor be destroyed in the chemical process. 4. Atoms of a particular element are same in all respects, i.e., they have same mass, size and chemical properties. 5. Atoms of one element are different from those of any other element, e.g., atoms of different elements can be distinguished from each other by their respective masses. 6. Atoms of different elements may combine in simple whole number ratio to form compound atoms (molecules) of a new substance. As per Dalton’s atomic theory, atom which is the smallest particle of an element, cannot be further divided and it retains all the characteristic properties of that element. 3.1 Dalton’s Atomic Theory and the Law of Conservation of Mass As per Dalton’s atomic theory, matter is made up of atoms which can neither be created nor destroyed. So, the number of different kinds of atoms in products of a chemical reaction must be same as the number of all kinds of atoms in reactants. Thus, the total mass of products of a chemical reaction is always equal to the total mass of reactants. 3.2 Dalton’s Atomic Theory and the Law of Constant Proportion As per Dalton’s atomic theory, each element is made up of atoms. The atoms of different elements combine together in whole numbers to give compound atoms of a new substance. Since the number and kind of atoms of each element in a compound are definite, masses of the constituent elements in a compound will be in a definite ratio. The law involved here is the law of constant proportion. Drawbacks of Dalton’s atomic theory are as follows : 1. The assumption that an atom is indivisible that is no longer true. An atom cart be decomposed into subatomic particles like electron, proton and neutron. 2. Atoms of the similar element may not be equal in all respects. items.stem: Neon (atomic number 10) neither transfers nor shares its valence electrons. Explain.
items.answer: Neon has an electronic configuration of 2, 8, which means its outermost shell is already completely filled with eight electrons. Because it already possesses a stable octet configuration, it does not need to gain, lose, or share any electrons, making it chemically unreactive and inert.

items.stem: What kind of ion will oxygen (O) form?
items.answer: Oxygen has an electronic configuration of 2, 6 and requires two more electrons to complete its octet. Therefore, it will gain two electrons to form a negatively charged anion with a valency of 2- (O2 -).

items.stem: Fill in the blanks. Among magnesium and chlorine, magnesium atom can give two electrons to become Mg2+. However, chlorine can take only one electron to become __________. Now, __________ ion of magnesium and __________ ions of chlorine combine to give magnesium chloride.
items.answer: Among magnesium and chlorine, magnesium atom can give two electrons to become Mg2+. However, chlorine can take only one electron to become a chloride ion (Cl-). Now, one ion of magnesium and two ions of chlorine combine to give magnesium chloride.

items.stem: Show the formation of cations of potassium (K) and calcium (Ca) atoms, and the formation of their corresponding chlorides using diagrams.
items.answer: For potassium chloride formation, depict a potassium atom losing its single valence electron to become a K+ cation, and a chlorine atom gaining that electron to become a Cl- anion. The strong electrostatic attraction between the single K+ and Cl- ions forms KCl. For calcium chloride formation, depict a calcium atom losing its two valence electrons to form a Ca2+ cation, and two separate chlorine atoms each accepting one of those electrons to form two Cl- anions. The electrostatic attraction between one Ca2+ ion and two Cl- ions forms CaCl2.

items.stem: Illustrate how sodium sulfide (Na2S) is formed.
items.answer: Sulfur has an electronic configuration of 2, 8, 6 and needs two electrons to achieve a stable octet, while sodium has a configuration of 2, 8, 1 and needs to lose one electron. Two sodium atoms each donate their single valence electron to one sulfur atom. This electron transfer results in two positively charged sodium cations (Na+) and one negatively charged sulfide anion (S2-), which are then held together by electrostatic forces to form sodium sulfide.

items.stem: An element X has six electrons in its outer shell and forms a diatomic molecule. (i) Why would that be so? (ii) What kind of bond would it form? (iii) Draw the structure of the molecule it would form. (iv) A certain other element Y has two electrons in its second shell. Draw the structure of the molecule that X would form with Y.
items.answer: (i) Element X has 6 valence electrons and needs 2 more to complete its stable octet configuration. By sharing two pairs of electrons with another atom of X, both atoms can achieve stability, resulting in the formation of a diatomic molecule (X2). (ii) Since it involves the sharing of electrons between atoms of the same element, it forms a covalent bond. Specifically, it forms a double covalent bond because two pairs of electrons are shared. (iii) (iv) Element Y has 2 valence electrons and will transfer them to element X (which needs 2 electrons) to form an ionic compound. To draw this, write the symbol Y with two dots next to it, and symbol X with six dots around it. Draw arrows from the two dots of Y pointing towards X to indicate electron transfer. Then, draw the resulting structure: a Y²+ ion (with no dots) positioned next to an X²- ion enclosed in square brackets [X]²- with 8 dots inside the brackets to show its completed octet.

items.stem: You want to design a new ionic compound, where the total positive charge is 6+ and the total negative charge is 6–. Which of the following combinations gives the correct number of ions? (i) 2 Al³+ and 3 Cl- (ii) 3 Mg²+ and 1 PO4³- (iii) 2 Fe³+ and 3 O²- (iv) 3 Ca²+ and 2 SO4²-
items.answer: (iii) 2 Fe³+ and 3 O²- is the correct option. The total positive charge from 2 iron ions is 2 × (+3) = +6, and the total negative charge from 3 oxide ions is 3 × (-2) = -6. This precisely matches the required 6+ and 6- charges to form a neutral compound (Fe2O3).

items.stem: Choose the correct statement(s) and correct the false statement(s). (i) Elements are made up of molecules and compounds are made up of atoms. (ii) The molecule of a compound is always made up of two or more atoms of the same kind. (iii) One molecule of nitrogen gas contains three nitrogen atoms. (iv) Water is made of two hydrogen atoms, covalently bonded with one oxygen atom.
items.answer: (i) This statement is false. Corrected statement: Elements are made up of atoms of the same kind, while compounds are made up of molecules or ions containing two or more different types of atoms combined in a fixed ratio. (ii) This statement is false. Corrected statement: The molecule of a compound is always made up of two or more atoms of different elements chemically bonded together. (iii) This statement is false. Corrected statement: One molecule of nitrogen gas (N2) is diatomic and contains exactly two nitrogen atoms. (iv) This statement is true. A water molecule (H2O) is formed by the sharing of electrons between one oxygen atom and two hydrogen atoms.

items.stem: The table lists the valencies of four hypothetical ions. A student uses the criss-cross method to write the chemical formulae for compounds formed by combining these specific ions. Which of the following chemical formulae is written correctly? Ion Symbol Type of Ion Valency X Cation 3 Y Cation 1 Z Polyatomic Anion 2 W Monoatomic Anion 1
items.answer: When determining chemical formulae, the valencies of combining ions are crossed over to become subscripts. Cation Y has a valency of one, and polyatomic anion Z has a valency of two. Crossing these gives two Y ions for every one Z ion, making the correct chemical formula Y2Z. The other options apply the valencies incorrectly.

Therefore, the incorrect assumption is that atoms of entirely distinct elements could somehow share the exact same physical mass and display identical chemical behaviour.

items.stem: If a species has 11 protons, 12 neutrons and 10 electrons then (i) what is its atomic number and mass number? (ii) is it neutral, a cation or an anion? Explain. (iii) write its electronic configuration. (iv) name the species.
items.answer: (i) The atomic number is the number of protons, which is 11. The mass number is the sum of protons and neutrons, which is 11 + 12 = 23. (ii) It is a cation. A neutral atom would have an equal number of protons and electrons (11 of each). Since this species has 11 positively charged protons but only 10 negatively charged electrons, it has a net positive charge of +1, making it a cation. (iii) Since it has 10 electrons, its electronic configuration is 2, 8. (iv) The atomic number 11 corresponds to the element Sodium. Because it has a +1 charge, the species is a sodium ion (Na+).

items.stem: Two elements, A and B, have the following configurations— A: 2, 8, 5 B: 2, 8, 7 (i) Which element is more reactive? (ii) Will A and B form ionic or covalent bonds when they combine? Explain using electron transfer or sharing. (iii) Predict the formula of the compound they would form.
items.answer: (i) Element B is more reactive. It has 7 valence electrons and only needs to gain or share one single electron to achieve a stable octet, which requires less energy and occurs much more readily than element A’s need to gain or share three electrons. (ii) Elements A and B will form covalent bonds when they combine. Both are non-metals that are short of electrons to complete their stable octets. Therefore, neither will transfer its electrons entirely; instead, they will share their valence electrons to achieve mutually stable electronic configurations. (iii) Element A needs 3 electrons (valency of 3), and element B needs 1 electron (valency of 1). By criss-crossing their valencies, the predicted formula for the resulting compound is AB3.

items.stem: Assertion (A): Copper sulfate conducts electricity in the molten state but not in the solid state. Reason (R): Copper and sulfate ions are fixed in the lattice in molten state, while in solid state they can move freely. Choose the correct option: (i) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. (ii) Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A. (iii) A is true, but R is false. (iv) A is false, but R is true.
items.answer: (iii) A is true, but R is false. The assertion is correct because ionic compounds like copper sulfate conduct electricity only when their ions are free to move. The reason is completely false because the states are reversed; ions are fixed in a crystal lattice in the solid state and become free to move only when the compound is in the molten or aqueous state.

items.stem: The species ²7Al, 30Br- and ²0¹Hg²+ have 13, 35 and 80 protons, respectively. How many electrons and neutrons do they have?
items.answer: For ²7Al (Neutral Aluminium atom): It has 13 protons. Since it is neutral, it has 13 electrons. The number of neutrons is Mass Number - Protons = 27 - 13 = 14 neutrons. For 30Br- (Bromide anion): It has 35 protons. The -1 charge means it has gained one electron, so it has 35 + 1 = 36 electrons. The number of neutrons is Mass Number - Protons = 80 - 35 = 45 neutrons. For ²0¹Hg²+ (Mercury cation): It has 80 protons. The +2 charge indicates it has lost two electrons, so it has 80 - 2 = 78 electrons. The number of neutrons is Mass Number - Protons = 201 - 80 = 121 neutrons. Atomic Foundations of Matter OBJECTIVE QUESTION
